summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and a history of anxiety was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She presented with lactic acidosis due to dehydration, elevated blood pressure attributed to her symptoms, and mild anemia. She was treated supportively with IV fluids, antiemetics, and insulin therapy. Her condition improved over two days, with resolution of acidosis, stabilization of blood pressure after restarting Lisinopril, and successful advancement to a full liquid diet. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume her home medications and follow up with GI and psychiatry for ongoing management.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Gastrointestinal malfunction arising from mental factors
Personal history of infections of the central nervous system
